chunks: From Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: If a man comes to the market and buys a cloak of fur but does not know whether it is pure or impure, can he pray in it? He said: Yes, you do not have to inquire about it, for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The Khawarij straitened things for themselves due to their ignorance; the religion is more expansive than that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in clothing of uncertain purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tahdhib illustrates the Shia principle of 'istishab al-hukm' (presumption of continuity), ruling that uncertainty regarding ritual purity does not invalidate prayer. Imam Abu Ja'far (AS) uses the Khawarij sect as a foil, contrasting their self-imposed rigor and ignorance with the inherent ease (yusr) of the true religion, thereby preventing excessive burden on the believers.
